practice.title: Living with Water
practice.passage:
For centuries, the people of the Netherlands have lived with a simple fact: about a quarter of their country lies below sea level. Rather than abandoning these lands, they built an elaborate system of dikes, canals, and pumps. Early farmers piled up earth mounds called terps to protect their homes from floods, and windmills, introduced in the fifteenth century, pumped water out of low-lying fields.

After a catastrophic storm flood in 1953 killed more than 1,800 people, the government launched the Delta Works, a series of dams and storm-surge barriers designed to shorten the coastline and reduce the risk of future floods. The project took more than forty years and is often described as one of the greatest feats of civil engineering.

In recent decades, however, engineers have changed their philosophy. Instead of only building higher walls, they now follow the principle of "Room for the River." Along several rivers, dikes have been moved inland and floodplains lowered so that rising water has space to spread out harmlessly. In some places, farmland has been converted into temporary wetlands. This approach is less expensive in the long term and also creates habitats for wildlife.

Experts believe that the Dutch experience offers valuable lessons for other countries facing rising seas, because it demonstrates that adaptation can be combined with nature rather than set against it.

items.q: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: The Netherlands built the Delta Works after a 1953 flood.
Dutch water management has shifted from only blocking water to working with natural processes.
Windmills were the most important invention in Dutch history.
Wetlands are cheaper than dikes everywhere in the world.
items.explain: Es la idea que unifica los tres primeros párrafos: de diques y barreras a «Room for the River». A y C son detalles; D generaliza demasiado.

items.q: How is the passage mainly organized?
options: A description of how an approach has changed over time
A list of problems without solutions
items.explain: Cronológico: terps y molinos → Delta Works (1953) → «Room for the River».

items.q: Why does the author mention terps in paragraph 1?
options: To show an early example of protecting homes from floods
To compare the Netherlands with other countries
items.explain: Terps son el primer ejemplo histórico de protección frente a inundaciones.

items.q: The word "feats" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
items.explain: «one of the greatest feats of civil engineering» = grandes logros.

items.q: According to paragraph 3, what does "Room for the River" involve?
options: Giving rising water space to spread out
Building new pumps near the coast
items.explain: «dikes have been moved inland and floodplains lowered so that rising water has space to spread out».

items.q: All of the following are mentioned in the passage EXCEPT
items.explain: Solar panels no aparecen. Molinos (p.1), Delta Works y la inundación de 1953 (p.2) sí.

items.q: What does the author imply about the "Room for the River" approach?
options: It is likely to be more sustainable in the long term
It has failed in several places
It is only useful in the Netherlands
It was proposed before the Delta Works
items.explain: Es «less expensive in the long term» y crea hábitats; el autor lo presenta como una lección valiosa.

practice.intro: Primero lee y escribe en una línea la idea principal; luego contesta.

quiz.q: Which part of a paragraph most often states its main point?
options: The topic sentence, often the first
quiz.explain: La oración temática suele abrir el párrafo.

quiz.q: The signal "In recent decades, however…" usually announces
quiz.explain: «however» + marca temporal anuncian un giro importante.

quiz.q: A "NOT/EXCEPT" question asks you to find the option that
options: does not appear in the passage
a complete statement covering the whole passage
quiz.explain: Debe cubrir todo el pasaje sin ser demasiado amplia ni estrecha.
